_comment: Dynamic inputs — videos, images, text. Changes each run. Actual files stored in stages/{stage}/data/.
_comment_items:
Per item name: {type, description, requires{}}. `requires` is THE CONTRACT — what the inference code will not run without — and it is what a candidate's `match` is judged against. Without it `mismatch` is a bare verdict that stops the workflow; with it, `mismatch` is a DIFF, which is simultaneously the spec for a conversion and the progress bar of one. `adaptation/adapt.py open` refuses a consumer whose items are empty for exactly that reason: nothing could say whether a round passed.

Fixed keys inside `requires`, each read out of the loading code rather than declared anywhere: `layout` (directory shape the code globs for), `annotation_format`, `fields` (name -> what the code expects that field to be), `value_ranges` (the constraints a loader will NOT raise on — an out-of-range category id is silently clamped, not a crash, which is why this is written down), `num_classes`, `evidence` (path:line).

A requirement that could not be read is `null`, never omitted: "the code does not care" and "nobody looked" are different facts, and only the first one makes a candidate's `ok` mean anything. Design reasoning: `lifecycle/references/roadmap.md` -> "Adaptation".

preprocessing._comment: MUST MATCH the training stage's input.json -> preprocessing on normalization / input_layout / label_transform — see lifecycle/references/run-mechanics.md 'Preprocessing contract (cross-stage)'. This is where train/serve skew lives: the model converges fine, inference returns plausible-looking output, and quality is quietly degraded with nothing to show in a log. `augmentation` must stay empty, or hold only explicitly-declared test-time augmentation.
